title.narrative: MSI Reproductive Choices - ASPIRE project support 2024-2028

description.narrative: Marie Stopes International har inkommit med en projektansökan, om 75 MSEK under perioden 2024-2028, för att genomföra ASPIRE projektet i Zambia. ASPIRE syftar till att förbättra tillgången och utnyttjandet av hälsovårdstjänster inom ramen för sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa. Projektet kommer att nå kvinnor, män och ungdomar med högkvalitativa, rättighetsbaserade och klientcentrerade tjänster inom sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa, för att förhindra oönskade graviditeter, osäkra aborter och i slutändan minska antalet dödsfall bland mödrar.

Marie Stopes International has submitted a project application for SEK 75 million during the period 2024-2028, to implement the ASPIRE project in Zambia. ASPIRE aims to improve access to -/and utilization of health services in particular SRHR services. The project will reach women, men and adolescents with high-quality, rights-based and client-centered sexual and reproductive health services to prevent unwanted pregnancies, unsafe abortions and ultimately reduce maternal deaths.

The overall goal of ASPIRE to contribute to reduced maternal mortality and morbidity and to improve womens health.
The project will reach women, men and adolescents with high-quality rights-based and client-centred sexual and reproductive health services, to avert unintended pregnancies, unsafe abortions and ultimately reduce the number of maternal deaths.

As it is the first year of implementation majority of activities have centered on preparing for longer term project activities. Nevertheless, some noticeable results have been achieved in the initial implementation phase (August/December 2024):
Through the new partnership with Tackle Africa, 48 peer educators (24 female and 24 male) between 1824 were trained to deliver Tackles football based HIV and SRHR intervention to their peers, challenging negative gender norms while integrating health messaging into football sessions with adolescent boys and young men. Tackle conducted 435 football sessions, reaching 1,129 adolescent boys and young men, this reflects 69% of the annual target due to a delay in the initial starting period.
Furthermore, MSZ has been working on strengthening existing service delivery channels and expanding access to essential SRHR services in three of the provinces that were supported under the previous project (Lusaka excluded), while setting up and expanding into Southern (the new province), ensuring access to SRHR information and services for predominantly rural, remote and marginalised communities. Through their new Accelerated Service Delivery Model (ASD) model, the outreach teams were able to provide services to 54 facilities in Eastern Province, 39 in Copperbelt, 90 in Southern Province and 62 in Northern Province. The achievement in Southern Province is impressive given that it is a new province, where MSZ did not have a presence before. In the first 6 months, they recorded 34,470 client visits and 34,477 services provided. A total of 130,711 Couple Years of Protection (CYP) was achieved in the same period. MSZ continued supporting the 56 public health facilities that were supported in the previous grant, where the sites recorded 101,381 visits. A total of 5,845 abortion and post abortion care services were provided and out of the total FP/Safe abortion client visits, 15% were adolescents aged 19 years or younger.
Additionally, MSZ has taken an active role in monitoring opposition against SRHR as well as addressing legal barriers to adolescent SRH access, such as Age of Consent. An Age of Consent Roadmap has since been created to work on a favourable approach for adolescent access to SRHR services.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
